recommended for most use cases and access patterns

evidence.quote: A general purpose bucket is a container for objects stored in Amazon S3, and you can store any number of objects in a bucket and across all storage classes (except for S3 Express One Zone), so you can redundantly store objects across multiple Availability Zones.

General purpose buckets are the original S3 bucket type, and a single general purpose bucket can contain objects stored across all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone. They are recommended for most use cases and access patterns.

claim: A directory bucket for low-latency use is created in a single Availability Zone and supports the S3 Express One Zone storage class; data is stored redundantly on multiple devices within that one Availability Zone, and the class is recommended for performance-sensitive applications that benefit from single-digit millisecond PUT and GET latencies.
question: What is a directory bucket with S3 Express One Zone, and how many Availability Zones does it use?

values.display: a single AWS Availability Zone

single-digit millisecond PUT and GET latencies

evidence.quote: For low-latency use cases, you can create a directory bucket in a single AWS Availability Zone to store data. Directory buckets in Availability Zones support the S3 Express One Zone storage class. With S3 Express One Zone, your data is redundantly stored on multiple devices within a single Availability Zone. The S3 Express One Zone storage class is recommended if your application is performance sensitive and benefits from single-digit millisecond `PUT` and `GET` latencies.

claim: S3 Object Ownership is a bucket-level setting. By default it is set to Bucket owner enforced and all ACLs are disabled; the bucket owner then owns every object in the bucket and manages access only with policies.
question: What is the default Object Ownership setting of a new bucket, and are ACLs on by default?

values.display: Bucket owner enforced
all ACLs are disabled
the bucket owner owns all the objects in the bucket

evidence.quote: S3 Object Ownership is an Amazon S3 bucket-level setting that you can use to both control ownership of the objects that are uploaded to your bucket and to disable or enable ACLs. By default, Object Ownership is set to the Bucket owner enforced setting, and all ACLs are disabled. When ACLs are disabled, the bucket owner owns all the objects in the bucket and manages access to them exclusively by using access-management policies.
